summary: Cross-region model-variant cache stampede causing 502/503 wave during tenant failover
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated tenant failover (us-east -> eu-west) for customer Currents AI on Dedicated, we observed a multi-minute wave of 502/503 responses originating at the API Gateway and amplified by upstream runtime restarts. Impact began at ~2026-03-12T18:03:00Z and resolved to baseline at ~2026-03-12T18:27:00Z after staged mitigations.

Impact:
- Customer observed ~60% elevated error rate for text and streaming requests for ~24k requests.
- Active streaming sessions dropped with reconnect storms.
- Throughput and tail latency degraded for other tenants on same reserved pool briefly; no SLA breaches reported yet but high user impact.

Timeline (high level):
- 18:02 UTC: Automated failover triggered by maintenance window (routing policy: region-fallback).
- 18:03 UTC: API Gateway error rate begins climbing; first 502 spikes seen.
- 18:05 UTC: Serving runtime autoscaler begins spinning up new shards in eu-west; several runtimes show rapid restarts.
- 18:08 UTC: KV cache miss rate and prefetch contention spikes; thrash on model-variant loads recorded.
- 18:12 UTC: Runtime watchdog OOM kills observed on a subset of nodes due to memory fragmentation while loading quantized variant.
- 18:18 UTC: Support mitigation applied (route pinning to warm model variant, reduced concurrency per-tenant).
- 18:27 UTC: Error rate returns to near-baseline.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-reserved-42 (GPU: A100-similar), private routing enabled for Currents AI.
- Control plane routing policy: region-fallback with model-variant auto-selection.

Steps to reproduce (approx, non-deterministic):
1) Initiate a region failover for a heavy tenant pinned to a quantized variant.
2) Ensure burst of concurrent long-prompt streaming sessions (~500 concurrent streams).
3) Observe kvcache miss amplification as model variant loads on many runtimes simultaneously.

Observed logs & signals:
- apigw: 502s with upstream reset: "upstream prematurely closed connection" correlating with runtime restarts.
- runtime: repeated model load logs: "loading model gptx-13b-quantized v12" followed by "alloc failed / fragmentation" and then watchdog exit.
- kvcache: spike in shard lock wait times (p95 lock wait 1.8s -> 12s).
- autoscaler: concurrent scale-up events with overlapping shard rebalancing.
- tracing: high latency in compile/kernel selection path during variant cold starts.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Primary hypothesis: Cross-region failover triggered simultaneous cold loads of the same quantized model variant across many runtimes. KV cache misses + model-prefetch attempts created a stampede; memory fragmentation on GPUs when loading quantized weights caused OOMs and runtime watchdog restarts, which in turn produced upstream resets to API Gateway.
- Secondary: Routing policy allowed mixed variant selection (quantized fallback) which caused incompatible kernel selection leading to additional latency and memory pressure.
- Tertiary: Autoscaler/backfill created overlapping restarts and accept-queue pressure on apigw leading to amplified 502s.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Pinned Currents AI traffic to pre-warmed quantized variant in us-east for 15 minutes (manual route override).
- Reduced tenant concurrency from 800 -> 200 on the impacted pool to limit memory contention.
- Disabled aggressive shard rebalancing for 10 minutes (scheduler throttle).
- Applied temporary kvcache backoff to serialize model prefetch for affected shard group.

Current status:
- Root cause work still in progress. Customer traffic stabilized; issue marked In Progress while engineering validates long-term fix.

Proposed long-term remediation items:
- Add staggered prefetch / leader election for model-variant loads on cross-region failovers to avoid stampedes.
- Improve GPU memory fragmentation handling during quantized weight allocations (driver/allocator retry & compaction).
- Make routing policy aware of ongoing warm state (avoid switching tenants to a region where variants are cold during heavy concurrency).
- Add autoscaler guard to prevent overlapping shard rebalances during tenant failover windows.

Customer communication plan:
- CS reached out to Currents AI at 2026-03-12T18:22Z with initial incident summary and mitigation steps; follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-14 to review root cause and roadmap for fixes.
